new_candidates.body:
### Is there an already existing issue for this?
- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Expected behavior
A participant that opens a shared-memory port segment left behind by a process killed while creating it discards the segment and creates it afresh. `open_port_internal` already does this for a segment with no port node, or one that fails its health check.

### Current behavior
`open_port_internal` never returns. The participant hangs inside `create_participant`, at 0% CPU, before it logs anything:

```
DomainParticipant::enable → RTPSParticipantImpl::setup_user_traffic → createReceiverResources
→ SharedMemTransport::OpenInputChannel → SharedMemManager::open_port
→ SharedMemGlobal::open_port_internal        (new SharedMemSegment(open_only, …))
→ managed_open_or_create_impl::priv_open_or_create
→ spin_wait::yield → nanosleep               (forever)
```

`managed_open_or_create_impl` creates a segment in steps:
1. create the file;
2. size it;
3. write `InitializingSegment` into its first word;
4. construct the segment manager;
5. write `InitializedSegment`.

A process killed between those steps leaves a file with no size, or with the first word still `UninitializedSegment` or `InitializingSegment`. The open path waits for the creator to finish, with no timeout, in `while(filesize == 0)` and in `while(value == InitializingSegment || value == UninitializedSegment)`. Fast DDS vendors Boost 1.73. Boost bounded both waits in 1.78 ([boostorg/interprocess#130](https://github.com/boostorg/interprocess/issues/130), [e4259fe](https://github.com/boostorg/interprocess/commit/e4259fe16804f5a4b179e1c7e69d201bd532d31a)).

The dead creator left no `_el` or `_sl` lock file, so `Port::is_zombie` returns false and the open goes ahead. Every process that later takes that port, meaning that participant ID on that domain, hangs the same way until someone deletes the file.

Bounding the wait alone is not enough. `open_port_internal`'s outer catch then calls `create_only`, which fails because the file still exists ("Failed to create port segment … File exists"), and the open throws "Couldn't open port".

### Steps to reproduce
1. Create `/dev/shm/fastrtps_port<N>` with no `_el` or `_sl` file, in one of two states:
   - with no size: `: > /dev/shm/fastrtps_port<N>`;
   - sized, with its first word set to 1, `InitializingSegment`: `printf '\x01\x00\x00\x00' > /dev/shm/fastrtps_port<N>; truncate -s 65536 /dev/shm/fastrtps_port<N>`.

   Here N is a port a participant will open as a SHM input channel: participant 0's user unicast port on domain D is 7400 + 250·D + 11.
2. Create a participant on domain D with SHM carrying user traffic. `create_participant` never returns.

With ROS 2 Jazzy, `ros2 run demo_nodes_cpp talker` on domain 199, with port 57161 planted, publishes nothing and has the stack above. The PR adds a unit test that plants each state.

### Fast DDS version/commit
2.14.6 (ROS 2 Jazzy binaries). The code is the same in master (980f19261).

### Platform/Architecture
Ubuntu Noble 24.04 amd64

### Transport layer
Shared Memory Transport (SHM)

### Additional context
In our CI, one launch's processes were aborted and SIGKILLed at teardown, and that left one such segment. Every later launch in the job lost one node, a different one each time, because a different process took that participant ID. We did not catch the kill itself.

The fix in the PR relies on the port mutex. A creator holds that mutex until the segment is initialized. So a segment that is still uninitialized after a short bound, while the mutex is held, had a creator that died. #6569 shows the mutex can be unlinked under a holder. In that case the existing `Couldn't find port_node` path already removes a live creator's segment one step later, with no grace period at all.
new_candidates.title: SHM: opening a port segment whose creator died before initializing it hangs forever
